an extensible benchmark for comparatively
evaluating memory architectures under poisoning attacks over long-horizon, multi-session trajectories.
Currently, MemoryDojo supports 155 multi-session trajectories covering 4 application domains, and
is enabled by 5 different agent memory system implementations. Additional memory systems,
environments, and configurations can be easily added for evaluation. We also introduce new metrics
to better quantify the effects of poisoning across its lifecycle, tracking information on payload
insertion, effects of persistence and propagation in memory, retrieval, and cumulative attack success
metrics. Finally, we propose a natural adaptive memory-aware poison optimization method that
performs iterative refinement of the payload prompt in an auxiliary environment.
Our experiments reveal substantial variation in poisoning success across memory systems.

2024) across four domains: Workspace, Travel, Banking, and Slack. Each domain provides a stateful

determines whether the objective is achieved. We concatenate tasks into trajectories, treating each task
execution as a separate session while carrying environment state forward. To ensure the concatenated
tasks remain executable, we check task pairs for state conflicts and validate each complete sequence.
For each domain, we also define an attacker objective ψ, accompanied by a textual description of
the behavior that the poison seeks to induce. Using these tasks and conversation histories from
LongMemEval-S (Wu et al., 2025), we obtain a dataset with three different collections.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation occurs on unseen MemoryDojo benchmark trajectories across four different models, with task utility and behavioral reach measured outside the auxiliary optimization environment.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are measured on held-out MemoryDojo trajectories across four application domains and history-prefixed sequences, using deterministic objective checks and session-level behavioral reach metrics.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Payloads are iteratively refined by an LLM optimizer using aggregate behavioral reach, memory lifecycle traces, and failure examples on synthetic trajectories in an auxiliary environment with disjoint tool names and task templates.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical findings directly align with the collected metrics, clearly demonstrating that memory architecture critically shapes poisoning persistence and downstream reach, and highlighting that auxiliary optimization generalizes across target domains and diverse model architectures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation systematically assesses five distinct memory systems (A-MEM, Graphiti, Letta, Mem0, Memora) across same-domain, cross-domain, and history-prefixed high-memory pressure settings, further cross-evaluating against four backbone language models (GPT-5.6-Luna, GPT-5.4-mini, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash) and measuring both attack success metrics and utility impacts.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is carried out on unseen MemoryDojo benchmark trajectories across four different models (GPT-5.6-Luna, GPT-5.4-mini, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash), measuring task utility and behavioral reach outside the auxiliary optimization environment.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Benchmark headline outcomes are measured on held-out MemoryDojo trajectories across four application domains and history-prefixed sequences, evaluated via deterministic objective checks and session-level behavioral reach (BR/BRT).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Payloads are iteratively refined by an optimizer model (GPT-5.6-Sol) using aggregate behavioral reach (BRT), memory lifecycle traces, and failure examples on synthetic trajectories inside an auxiliary environment with disjoint tool names and tasks.

primary.limitations: The work explicitly documents key boundaries, including restricting tasks to sandboxed environments, single-point poison insertion, evaluation on five specific open-source memory configurations, and leaving multi-injection attacks and defensive countermeasure designs for future research.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formalizing trajectory execution over retrieve-interact-write cycles, tracking memory insertion/retrieval/persistence/propagation, and optimizing payloads using an LLM in an auxiliary environment with disjoint tools and tasks to evaluate cross-environment transfer.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides clear experimental controls, detailed lifecycle metrics, rigorous ablation across domains and models, and an auxiliary-to-evaluation transfer setup that prevents circular evaluation.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces MemoryDojo, an extensible empirical benchmark and framework of 155 multi-session trajectories across four application domains designed to trace the lifecycle, persistence, propagation, and behavioral reach of indirect prompt poisoning across five representative LLM agent memory architectures.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides clear experimental controls, detailed lifecycle metrics, rigorous ablation across domains and models, and an auxiliary-to-evaluation transfer setup that prevents circular evaluation.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The work explicitly documents key boundaries, including restricting tasks to sandboxed environments, single-point poison insertion, evaluation on five specific open-source memory configurations, and leaving multi-injection attacks and defensive countermeasure designs for future research.

concerns: The core proposed mechanism, cross-expert attribution for cold-expert mitigation, is explicitly neither implemented nor evaluated, so the central scientific claim remains unvalidated.

The headline PROFYBENCH-V1 result relies on a single o3-mini LLM judge without human or independent ground-truth verification, and the auxiliary four-model audit is explicitly not used to validate results because its aggregate definition and paired records are unavailable.

The benchmark evaluates only the aggregate Full configuration and does not test cold-expert mitigation, cross-expert transfer, or longitudinal distillation, leaving the paper's titular contribution unsupported by the reported experiments.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the authors provide commendable transparency about what is implemented versus proposed, the paper's primary conceptual contributions (cross-expert attribution and cold-expert resolution) are entirely unexecuted and unevaluated.
